accuracy.evidence: Q = I t, units and the series-loop statement are taken from AQA 8463 section 4.2.1.3 wording. The electrons-per-coulomb figure was computed from the exact SI elementary charge (1 / 1.602176634e-19 = 6.242e18). Every lab number was checked: 2 A × 3 s = 6 C; 12 C ÷ 3 A = 4 s and ÷ 1.5 A = 8 s exactly (the finish check compares exact values); 0.5 A × 300 s = 150 C; 0.2 A × 120 s = 24 C; 3,000 C ÷ 10 A = 300 s; slopes 20 C/10 s = 2 A and 35 C/10 s = 3.5 A; loop 10 C in 5 s = 2 A; challenge 0.4 × 120 = 48 C and 0.25 × 20 = 5 C.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented errors: not converting minutes/hours and mA before substituting (scene 3 with slip-specific distractors 2.5 C, 400 C, 24,000 C; challenge 'mins' and 'milli'), inverting the rearrangement (0.003 s, 0.08 C, 'flip'), current used up by a lamp (Shipstone 1984; Driver et al. 1994; scene 5 prediction and challenge 'used'), confusing current with energy per charge ('volt'), and misreading gradient on a Q-t graph (scene 4 prediction).

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanism is charge per unit time: a counting gate on a wire whose dot flux equals I ÷ 0.5 C per second, a stopwatch that stops at a fixed charge, a charge-time graph whose dragged slope is the current, and a counting ring moved round a loop. flagcirc teaches current and voltage readings, flagcurdir direction, flagacdc waveforms; none count coulombs against time.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds the rule by doing: the counter shows Q growing as I × t and only 2 A gives 6 C in 3 s; with Q fixed they see 3 A take 4 s and 1.5 A take 8 s, so halving the current doubles the time; the graph only accepts the slope equal to the asked current; the ring reads the same 2 A at four points before the text says charge is not used up.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 2 A for 3 s (1.5 C from dividing, 5 C from adding, vs 6 C), halving current (time halves vs doubles), steeper Q-t line (smaller current vs bigger), and current after the lamp ('the lamp uses some up' vs the same).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Eight distinct messages keyed to the slip: 'times' (multiplied instead of dividing), 'flip' (division upside down, check C/s), 'mins' (120 s), 'used' (charge not used up, lamp takes energy), 'milli' (0.25 A), 'volt' (energy per coulomb is p.d.), 'graph' (gradient is current), plus the default unit reminder. Scene 3 also gives a worked correction for every wrong option.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes the learner kid limit (6.5) and adult limit (9.5). Kid paragraphs are short sentences with one idea each and a worked number in each (two amps for three seconds, five minutes is 300 seconds, 200 mA is 0.2 A); curriculum terms (coulomb, ampere, rate of flow) are defined at first use.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passes. Each kid paragraph gives a definition, a worked example or a rule; adult text gives the specification reference, the SI definition with the exact elementary charge, named mistakes and a lab summary. No template sentences shared with other lessons (explanation similarity under 12%).

mobile.evidence: Narrow canvas ratio 1.15 at 390 px; every readout uses a shrink-to-fit tag; the current handle grabs within a 30 px band, the graph end grabs anywhere in the right 40% of the plot, the loop ring snaps to the nearest wire point within 36 px; answer tiles are at least 56 px tall. Phone screenshots of all steps were checked and the walk gate runs on iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: Button twins for every canvas action: Less current / More current / Run, an answer button per unit-trap option, Less steep / Steeper / Check line, and Point A-D for the loop. All results go through c.say and the canvas aria-label; challenge feedback is a polite live region; the loop animation stops under reduced motion. axe WCAG 2.1 AA is run in both themes on desktop and phone by the walk gate.
